papers.title: Character Correspondents for Finite Groups

coverage.read: Official SIAM HTML mathematical main text sections 1-7 read; official 10-page PDF title, authors, venue and selected passages checked using web PDF text extraction.
integrated: Sections 2-4: A5 example, Clifford restriction, Frattini diamond, associated projective representations, factor-set and central triple relations, relative degree theorem, inductive McKay condition, reduction theorem and route.
Sections 5-6: blocks, defect groups, heights, Brauer correspondence, height-zero theorem and explicit proof-route limitations.
Sections 5.4 and 7: Galois-McKay, weights, Alperin weight conjecture, character fields, conductors and Feit conjecture.

Deepening 2026-09-23: omitted Glauberman branch in finite abelian coprime-action case, full fixed-point and normalizer orbit arguments, complete split abelian-kernel/abelian-Sylow McKay calculation, C3^2 swap and C2^2 semidirect C3 examples.

Complete ordinary/projective Clifford infrastructure: averaging, isotypic evaluation, character inner products, induction correspondence, construction of associated multiplier, inverse-multiplier classification, relative degree and Gallagher proofs, cyclic quotient extensions and explicit Q8 obstruction.
coverage.proof_level: Historical first-pass scope retained in first_pass_coverage. Current deepening fully proves the finite complex Clifford and projective multiplicity classification and the bounded abelian/split correspondence cases listed in deepening.complete_proofs. No general Glauberman, general solvable McKay, CFSG verification or deep block proof is claimed.

limitations: No exact arXiv version of this conference report was found; a different Malle-Navarro-Tiep survey was not substituted.

General nonabelian Glauberman correspondence remains unproved; the abelian case is now fully proved. Dade's alternating-chain conjecture, full block relation >=_b, detailed inductive Feit condition and A6 remain unexpanded.

McKay and height-zero results are theorems; general Alperin-McKay, Alperin weight, Galois-McKay and Feit statements retain conjecture status as in the read report.

complete_proofs.scope: For a symmetric set X containing 1, N normal and N subset X^c, quotient width m implies generated-subgroup width at most m+c; includes counterexample if the kernel assumption is dropped.
For any abelian group, a word with exponent sums e_i has value set gcd(e_i)A, including the all-zero case; Bezout proof and exact width 0 or 1.
For a profinite group, abstract verbal width equals the supremum of finite continuous quotient widths; compactness, finite intersections, and closedness under a uniform finite bound are proved.

Given a nonidentity SL2(Z) word value, explicit block commutators and a Bezout change of basis put every e13(tq) in two symmetric word values. This does NOT establish existence of the initial nonidentity word value.
Surjectivity SL_n(Z) -> SL_n(Z/dZ), n>=2; local Gaussian elimination, elementary diagonal identities, and an explicit Chinese remainder construction.
Maschke complete reducibility for finite-dimensional complex representations, by averaging a projection and induction on dimension.
Canonical isotypic decomposition, evaluation U tensor Hom_N(U,V) -> V_U, and the correspondence between submodules of an isotypic module and multiplicity subspaces.
Character inner product equals Hom dimension via averaging on matrix space; irreducible orthogonality, multiplicities, and character determination of semisimple complex representations.
Full proof of 0174: transitivity of G on N-isotypic components, equal multiplicities, and the restriction/degree formula for finite complex representations.
Induction construction, dimension and complete coset-trace character formula; not a proof of all general induction theorems.
Clifford inertia-subgroup induction bijection; proves irreducibility, surjectivity, inverse by theta-isotypic component, and degree formula.
Existence of an associated projective representation for every finite character triple via a section and intertwiners; computes the quotient cocycle and normalization.

Full inverse-multiplier multiplicity-space classification: action formula, descent to quotient, cancellation, evaluation inverse, submodule/irreducibility equivalence and isomorphism-class injectivity.
Full proof of 0179 using the now-proved 01J7; common inverse-multiplier parameter gives a bijection, relative degree equality and p'-degree restriction with stated degree assumptions.
Gallagher correspondence using 01J7 with multiplier one, including product-character and dimension calculation.
Coprime finite action on a finite abelian group K: averaging projection proves K=C_K(A) direct sum [A,K], identifies image and kernel, without a general coprime-action theorem.
All finite abelian irreducibles are linear and the dual has size |K|, proved using Schur and the regular representation.
Full proof of theorem 01JB: A-invariant linear characters are exactly those trivial on [A,K], restriction is bijective, inverse is composition with averaging, and commuting-automorphism equivariance.
Finite p-group fixed-point congruence |X|=|X^P| mod p, via orbit-stabilizer and Lagrange.
N_G(P) transitivity on fixed points in a transitive G-set, provided P is Sylow and fixed points exist; Sylow conjugacy in a point stabilizer is the explicit named elementary input.
Explicit C3^2 coordinate-swap Glauberman map lambda_(a,a) -> mu_(2a), and its inverse; all character parameters computed.
Complete McKay bijection for K semidirect P with K finite abelian p' and P abelian p-group; inertia extensions, all degrees, normalizer C_K(P) times P, and the correspondence are proved.
Full character table of C2^2 semidirect C3, with conjugacy classes, induced values, inner products, and the p=3 McKay map.

Q8 central sign character: explicit nontrivial multiplier, inverse-multiplier matrices, uniqueness/irreducibility of the two-dimensional representation, character values, and obstruction to a linear extension.
Extension of invariant complex irreducible characters across a finite cyclic quotient using scalar normalization of an intertwiner; verifies the group law and irreducibility.
